record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: For sufficiently fast flow through a porous medium, how do pore shape and tortuosity determine the coefficients and validity of a nonlinear Darcy law, including whether turbulence at the pore scale can arise and whether Darcy's law can fail as a deterministic macroscopic law?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a periodic porous medium $\Omega_\varepsilon \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ ($d=2,3$) obtained as follows: let $Y=(0,1)^d$ be the unit cell, let $Y_s \subset Y$ be a closed solid inclusion with smooth boundary, and set $Y_f = Y \setminus Y_s$ (the fluid part, assumed connected). For $\varepsilon>0$, let $\Omega_\varepsilon$ be the $\varepsilon$-periodic perforation of a bounded domain $\Omega$ obtained by removing $\varepsilon$-scaled copies of $Y_s$. Inside $\Omega_\varepsilon$ consider an incompressible viscous fluid governed by the stationary Navier–Stokes equations
$$-\mu \Delta u_\varepsilon + \rho (u_\varepsilon \cdot \nabla) u_\varepsilon + \nabla p_\varepsilon = f, \qquad \mathrm{div}\, u_\varepsilon = 0,$$
with no-slip boundary conditions $u_\varepsilon=0$ on $\partial Y_s^\varepsilon$, where $\mu,\rho>0$ are fixed and the pore Reynolds number $\mathrm{Re}_p$ is order one or larger (the "sufficiently fast" regime where linear Darcy theory no longer applies).

Let $\langle u_\varepsilon \rangle$ denote the macroscopic Darcy velocity (the volume average of $u_\varepsilon$) and $\nabla P$ the homogenized pressure gradient. A nonlinear Darcy law is any deterministic constitutive relation
$$\nabla P = F(\langle u_\varepsilon \rangle)$$
obtained as the homogenized limit $\varepsilon\to 0$, where $F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ depends on the cell geometry $Y_s$ (encoding pore shape and tortuosity).

Answer the following:

(a) Determine explicitly how the geometry of $Y_s$ — in particular the pore shape and the tortuosity of the connected fluid channels — enters the coefficients of $F$, including the leading-order inertial correction beyond linear Darcy (e.g. whether $F$ takes Forchheimer form $\nabla P = -A\,\langle u\rangle - B(\langle u\rangle)|\langle u\rangle|$).

(b) Identify the range of pore Reynolds numbers (in terms of $\varepsilon$, $\mu$, $\rho$, and the geometry) within which such a deterministic nonlinear Darcy law is valid.

(c) Decide whether turbulence at the pore scale can develop within the cell problem under steady macroscopic forcing, and if so, whether such pore-scale turbulence forces the macroscopic relation between $\langle u_\varepsilon\rangle$ and $\nabla P$ to fail as a deterministic (single-valued) law — i.e. whether the homogenized limit must instead be described stochastically or multi-valuedly.
artifact.status_search_result: Rigorous homogenization derivations of the Forchheimer (quadratic) correction to Darcy's law from Navier–Stokes in periodic perforated domains are known (Mikelić and coworkers), and the dependence of the nonlinear coefficient on pore geometry/tortuosity has been studied numerically and asymptotically. However, the precise range of validity at higher Reynolds numbers, the rigorous treatment of pore-scale turbulence within the homogenization framework, and whether Darcy-type laws fail as deterministic macroscopic laws in turbulent pore regimes remain open.

status_evidence.title: Derivation of the Forchheimer Law via Homogenization
status_evidence.snippet: Justification of the Forchheimer law starting from the pore scale Navier–Stokes equations via homogenization.
status_evidence.claim: The quadratic Forchheimer-type nonlinear Darcy law has been rigorously derived via homogenization for moderate Reynolds numbers.

status_evidence.title: The Transition from Darcy to Nonlinear Flow in Heterogeneous Porous Media
status_evidence.snippet: Disordered pore morphology gives rise to highly non-uniform flow fields similar to turbulent flow, with coherent topological patterns at the transition.
status_evidence.claim: The transition to turbulent-like pore-scale flow and its impact on macroscopic laws is an active area, suggesting deterministic Darcy-type laws may fail at higher Reynolds numbers.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization of non-Darcy flow in porous media containing spheroidal impervious inclusions
status_evidence.snippet: Homogenization analysis of non-Darcy flow with geometric inclusion shape dependence.
status_evidence.claim: Dependence of nonlinear Darcy coefficients on pore shape is being actively quantified via homogenization.
